title: Kaption game manifest
description: One file per game: games/<id>.json, where the file name is the wire id. Read by the desktop (embedded at build time), the site, the backend catalog and the updater tests. Validate with: node tools/games/validate.cjs

id.description: Wire id: R2 keys, D1 `game`, CLI --game, the bundle's game. Always gameId lower-cased. Never changes.

gameId.description: Desktop GameId: Config["Game"], the %APPDATA%\Kaption\<gameId>\ folder and the Game_<gameId> string key. Never changes.

shortName.description: Label for tight spots (the site's game chips).

status.description: planned: catalog and vote only. beta, live: desktop and site. withdrawn: nowhere.

aliases.description: Other spellings of gameId that Config.json may hold. They resolve to this game's desktop profile.

legacyIds.description: Other wire ids older tools used for this game (starrail was hsr). Only the loose lookups (art, accents) read them; desktop profile lookup never does.

name.description: The game's own English name for it (Original Resin, Reserved Trailblaze Power).

regenSeconds.description: Seconds per point while under max.

stamina.description: The game's stamina and how it refills: the site's stamina timer reads it. Every value is checked against the game data of `checked.version` where that data carries it (`checked.ref`), else against the game's own item text or published sources.

hold.description: The most the player can hold through refills and rewards (regeneration pauses above max). Absent when the data does not say.

reserve.description: A second pool that fills only while the main one is at max (Reserved Trailblaze Power, Backup Battery Charge, Waveplate Crystals).

version.description: The game version whose data or text was checked.

ref.description: Where: a table and key, an item text, or a source.

rect.description: A region as fractions of the 16:9 reference area inside the game window.

requireTitle.description: true: a process counts as the game only while one of its windows has a title from windowTitles. For generic engine executables such as Unreal's Client-Win64-Shipping. Absent means false.

pacing.description: Per-game OCR pacing defaults. A key left out means the global default (GameOcrTuning). Bounds are the resolver's clamp.

vision.description: Every key optional; a key left out keeps the shipping (accent) default.

classifier.description: Speaker/body split. accent: the name is in an accent colour. geometry: the name is the narrow top row (name and body share a colour). speaker-row: the name is the top row of a centred dialogue column, accent-coloured or in a larger font; rows that start right of the column are side panels.

ocrJunkFilter.description: Drop HUD readouts, watermarks and stray glyphs (OcrTextJunkFilter) before the speaker/body split on every frame. The geometry classifier always does.

dialogueEvidence.description: Paint a match only when the dialogue data vouches for it: a dialogue-graph line, or a known speaker saying something that reads as speech. Map labels, menus and item text are TextMap keys too.

fadedReadFilter.description: Treat a read whose body boxes are barely lit (under 2% of pixels past the binary threshold) as empty: the line is fading out, and keeping it would hide the fade from the change gate.

sessionCheck.description: How much evidence the Start card needs before it says why no line shows. A key left out keeps the app's default (GameRegionProfile); 0 switches that sentence off for the game.

blackSeconds.description: Seconds of unbroken black frames with the game in front, before any line was found in this run of translation: the game looks like exclusive full screen. Default 30.

unmatchedReads.description: Different spoken lines (a speaker and a sentence) read in a row without one pack hit: is the game's text in English? Default 20.

quietSeconds.description: Seconds with the game in front and nothing dialogue-like read, on an install that has not shown a line yet. Default 60.

dialogueContext.description: Dialogue strategy set. Only passthrough exists; anything else fails closed like an unknown game.

upstreamTextMap.description: Runtime TextMap mirror for the source languages. none: the bundle carries the map (minted key space).

displayModeTip.description: The one-time display-mode tip before the first start.

playerNameTokens.description: The player's default name as the subtitle text spells it, each replaced by the name set in Settings. Left out: Traveler and traveler, the app's behaviour before manifests.

notes.description: For maintainers: which values are measured and which are provisional. No consumer reads it.

staminaScreen.description: Where the game draws its stamina number ("160/200" beside the stamina icon) and how the desktop reads it, for a player who switched that on. Present only for a game measured on real frames (`measured`); without it the feature is off for the game. `search` is in fractions of the game's client area (not the 16:9 band: the pill is anchored to the window's edge); the icon template is drawn for a 1920x1080 client.

search.description: The part of the client area the icon can be in.

scales.description: Icon sizes tried, relative to the template: one game draws the icon larger on its map than in its dialogs, and the interface scale of an unmeasured aspect ratio may differ a little.

minIconScore.description: Lowest template score (normalised correlation) that counts as the icon.

digits.description: The number's place to the right of the icon.

width.description: How far right of the icon the number can reach, in icon heights.

maxStart.description: The furthest right of the icon the number may start, in icon heights (a right-aligned number moves with its length).

inkLevel.description: A pixel is ink at this share of the brightest pixel beside the icon; dividers and pill borders are dimmer.

maxGap.description: The widest gap inside the number, in digit heights; a wider one ends it (the "+" button).

minTextScore.description: Lowest recognition confidence for the number.

sampleSeconds.description: How often the app looks, while subtitles run and the game is in front.

confirmations.description: Agreeing samples before a number that differs from the timer's is believed.

refillConfirmations.description: The same for a number higher than regeneration explains (a refill).

version.description: The game version of the frames it was measured on.

ref.description: Which screens, at which sizes, and where the record is.

accent.description: The game's accent on dark surfaces (site, desktop dark palette).

accentDark.description: The accent deepened for light surfaces (desktop light palette). Defaults to accent.

glow.description: The Start hero's glow behind the art. Defaults to accent.

signal.description: The game's colour where its mark is small on the site (a 20 px tile, a chip): set it when the accent does not read there. Defaults to accent.

elementHues.description: Element colours this game draws differently from the shared table, or adds (English element names).

hub.description: Public URL slug. Never changes for an existing game.

guideKey.description: guide-pages.ts key of the game's guide (honkai for Star Rail).

ogBackground.description: Key art for generated update images, relative to landing/.

mark.description: The game's drawn mark on the site: an SVG of ours on a 24 unit grid, one colour, relative to landing/. Never a logo. Without it the game's initial stands on the tile.

motif.description: The thin pattern behind the game's typographic leads on the site.

guessName.description: The daily guessing game's own name on the site (Gendle). Unique across games.

upcoming.description: How a character that is not out yet shows on the site, in the content API, the Discord bot and the desktop bundle. full (the default when absent): announced with its whole kit. teaser: name, portrait, element, weapon type and release day only, until 00:00 UTC of its own day; a character without a known day is not shown. hide: nothing until that day. A day that is only the version's first day never opens a kit (the next version going live does), and a section without release information is never served whole. See games/README.md.

currency.description: The game's premium currency in English, as players search for codes with it (Primogems): the codes pages put it in their titles.

library.description: The binding of this game's books on the site (the reading view of a series part and the library): two pages, their inks, the colour of ornaments on each, an ornament set and a cover material. Without it the game reads on the site's own Night and Paper with the plain ornaments. tools/games/validate.cjs checks every pair's contrast.

ink.description: Text on the lit page: 10:1 or more, so secondary text mixed toward the page still reads.

night.description: The night page (the Night tone, the default).

nightInk.description: Text on the night page: 10:1 or more.

mark.description: Ornaments, the chapter numeral and the drop cap on the lit page: 3:1 or more. Defaults to look.accentDark, then look.accent.

nightMark.description: The same on the night page. Defaults to look.accent.

ornament.description: The ornament set (landing/src/data/library-look.ts ORNAMENTS): the mark between sections, the end mark, the corner pieces and the page's faint pattern.

binding.description: The cover material of the game's books in the library (landing/src/components/library/BookCover.astro).

sources.description: auto: the VPS updater's packs. community: accepted player suggestions.

hoyolabGid.description: HoYoLAB game id; null off HoYoLAB.

officialFeeds.description: Official news sources the news worker reads, keyed by kind.

oneOf.description: An official YouTube channel (its RSS feed).
Kuro Games' official site news list (JSON).

codes.description: null: the game has no redeem codes. hoyolab: the news worker reads the HoYoLAB codes panel and the site has a codes page with a redeem link. ingame: codes are redeemed only inside the game; the site's codes page shows Copy and the in-game steps (redeemHow) instead of a link, and the news worker reads the sources [news.games.<id>] names (the official Discord follow, the wiki, the checked list).

officialDiscord.description: The game's official Discord server (guild id). Messages its announcement channels crosspost into the channel [news.games.<id>] discord_follow names are an official codes source next to the HoYoLAB panel; nothing else in that channel is.

redeemHow.description: Where a code is entered inside the game, as the game's own English UI labels: the site and the code alerts word the steps per language around them.

path.description: The menus from the main screen to the code field, in order (Terminal, Settings, ...).

unlock.description: The progress that unlocks the code field (Union Level 2), English game terms; absent when it is open from the start.

officialDiscord.description: The game's official Discord server (guild id). Messages its announcement channels crosspost into the channel [news.games.<id>] discord_follow names are an official codes source; nothing else in that channel is.
